A Generalized Linear Model (GLM) with a Binomial distribution and Logit link function is recommended for 'Success'.     "Homogeneity of variances across stimulation groups (Levene's test or Bartlett's test).",
    "Homogeneity of slope (if using regression) or homogeneity of variance-covariance matrices (if using MANOVA).",
    "For 'Success', check for separation or extreme proportions in small groups (though Sham has n=3505, so likely fine)."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Based on summary statistics, 'Sham' is expected to show significantly worse performance (higher Time-to-Target, lower Success, lower Path Efficiency, lower Average Speed, lower AD) compared to all other paradigms.",

    "Time-to-Target is expected to be shortest for 'Combined' (2.56) and longest for 'Sham' (4.68).",
    "Success is expected to be significantly lower for 'Sham' (0.27) compared to others (0.67-0.78).",
    "Path Efficiency is expected to be highest in visual/combined conditions and lowest in Sham (0.31 vs 0.43-0.50).",
    "Average Speed is expected to be lowest in Sham (10.74) and highest in Combined (12.83).",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion) is expected to be lowest in Sham (0.24) and highest in Combined (0.40), suggesting less consistent turning or more erratic paths in Sham, or conversely, tighter turns in Sham (depending on AD definition, but statistically distinct from others)."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The dataset appears to be repeated measures (multiple trials per mouse), but the summary suggests a One-Way ANOVA plan. A Mixed Effects Model accounting for 'Mouse' as a random intercept is more statistically rigorous and will reduce Type I error inflation.",
    "The 'Success' variable is binary; analyzing it with standard ANOVA assumes normality which is violated. A GLM or transformation is necessary for valid inference.",
    "The large sample size (n=76,655) may lead to statistically significant results for trivial effect sizes; effect size metrics are critical.",
    "Potential outliers in 'Time-to-Target' (max=201 vs mean=2.8) could skew means and ANOVA results; robust methods or log-transformation may be needed.",

Compare model fit using AIC/BIC and visualize estimated marginal means with 95% confidence intervals for all paradigms."
}
